title: Saraburi to Khao Yai 2D1N Road Trip — Cross-Province Drive Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Drive from Bangkok through Saraburi (Phra Phutthabat Temple, Muak Lek Waterfall, Thai-Danish Farm) then continue to Khao Yai and Pak Chong on day two. Real routes, timings, and current prices.
keywords: Saraburi Khao Yai trip, Khao Yai 2 days 1 night itinerary, Saraburi Pak Chong road trip, drive to Khao Yai
intro: Saraburi and Khao Yai sit along the same highway — Mittraphap Road (Highway 2) — which makes pairing them into a cross-province trip surprisingly logical. Day one, you pick up Saraburi's highlights along the way: Phra Phutthabat Temple, Muak Lek Waterfall, and the Thai-Danish Dairy Farm. Spend the night around Muak Lek or Pak Chong. Day two, push up into Khao Yai National Park in the morning cool, then wind down the afternoon on the Pak Chong side with vineyards, farms, and European-feel cafés. No backtracking — this plan follows the road in one clean line.

blocks.html: The beauty of combining Saraburi with Khao Yai is that you never have to choose between them. Driving north from Bangkok on Mittraphap Road (Highway 2), you pass through central Saraburi, then Kaeng Khoi, Muak Lek, and finally Pak Chong and Khao Yai — all strung along the same corridor. Bangkok to Pak Chong is roughly 180–200 km, about 2.5–3 hours non-stop. This trip builds in proper stops along the way rather than racing past.

This itinerary is designed for people with their own car or a rental. The attractions are spread out and awkward to reach by public transport. No car? Take a bus or minivan to Pak Chong, then rent a car locally or hire a day-use van from a local operator.

Day one treats Saraburi not as a destination you rush past, but a place worth a proper morning and afternoon. Leave Bangkok early, stop at the temple, swim at the waterfall, pop into the dairy farm, then check in near Muak Lek or Pak Chong before dark.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Bangkok → Saraburi → Overnight in Muak Lek / Pak Chong

items.activity: Leave Bangkok — head north on Mittraphap Road
items.note: Early start helps you clear the Rangsit–Saraburi stretch before traffic builds. It's about 110 km to central Saraburi.
Saraburi's most revered site — climb the mondop to pay respects at the sacred Buddha footprint. Free entry; dress modestly. Budget about an hour.
A single-drop waterfall that pools into a wide rock basin — great for wading in cool water. Entry is a few dozen THB. Bring non-slip shoes and a change of clothes.
The Muak Lek area has noodle shops, som tam stalls, and riverside spots. A decent break before the afternoon push.
Thailand's first dairy farm, run by the Agricultural Promotion Organization. There's a tractor tour, a cow-feeding activity, and their own ice cream and fresh milk shop. Good for families.

items.activity: Café or hilltop viewpoint near Muak Lek
items.note: The Muak Lek–Pak Chong corridor has a lot of mountain-view cafés. A quiet coffee stop before checking in is a good way to decompress.

items.activity: Check in — Muak Lek or Pak Chong side
items.note: Staying this side puts you close to Khao Yai's gate in the morning. Details on the best location in the tip below.

items.activity: Dinner — wagyu BBQ or grilled pork Khao Yai-style
items.note: Pak Chong has plenty of good wagyu and mu kratha (Thai BBQ) spots. Comfortable close to day one.

blocks.title: Choosing where to sleep
blocks.html: If your main goal on day two is getting into Khao Yai early, pick accommodation near Pak Chong or along Route 2090 (Thanarat Road), which leads straight to the national park gate. That saves roughly an hour of driving compared with staying in central Saraburi and having to drive back up in the morning.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Saraburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Saraburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: Day two is the highlight. Go up into Khao Yai National Park while it's still cool in the morning — that's when you're most likely to spot wildlife and catch mist on the ridges. By early afternoon, come back down to the Pak Chong side for vineyards, farms, and that Tuscan-village-in-Thailand moment before driving home.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khao Yai National Park → Pak Chong → Back to Bangkok

items.activity: Enter Khao Yai National Park (Pak Chong gate)
items.note: Thai adults 40 THB, children 20 THB, plus a vehicle fee. Gate opens 08:00 — arriving early means cooler air and better chances of seeing wildlife on the road.

items.activity: Km 30 Viewpoint / Pha Diao Dai Overlook
items.note: A mountain-sea panorama across Khao Yai's ridges — morning mist makes this even better. The Pha Diao Dai trail involves proper hiking; check in with park staff before setting out.
Khao Yai's most famous waterfall. Short walk from the car park. In the rainy season the flow is powerful and photogenic; in the dry season it's calmer but still worth it.

items.activity: Drive down — lunch on the Pak Chong side
items.note: Head back down to Pak Chong and grab a meal at a restaurant or café with a proper kitchen before the afternoon.

items.activity: Chokchai Farm or PB Valley Khao Yai Winery
items.note: Chokchai Farm runs guided tours with cow-milking activities. PB Valley is a working vineyard with tractor tours and wine tasting. Pick one based on your group — check tour times in advance for both.

items.activity: Primo Piazza or another European-style café in Pak Chong
items.note: Primo Piazza replicates a Tuscan village, complete with alpacas, sheep, and goats. Entry is about 100 THB for adults, 50 THB for kids. Best for photos in soft afternoon light.
Try to leave before it gets late — Mittraphap Road heading south on Sunday evenings can get heavy. The drive back is about 180–200 km.

items: Bangkok → Saraburi — Take Mittraphap Road (Hwy 2) north through Rangsit and Pratu Nam Phra In. About 110 km to central Saraburi.
Saraburi → Muak Lek → Pak Chong — Continue north on Hwy 2 through Kaeng Khoi and Muak Lek to Pak Chong. Total from Bangkok is about 180–200 km.
Pak Chong → Khao Yai National Park — Turn onto Route 2090 (Thanarat Road) and drive up to the Pak Chong gate. The road is winding and steep — take it slow.
No car option — Bus or minivan from Bangkok to Pak Chong, then rent a car locally or hire a day-use minivan driver for touring.

blocks.title: Driving the mountain road safely
blocks.html: The road up Khao Yai is steep with a lot of tight bends. Check your brakes and tyres before you leave. Use a low gear on the way down rather than riding the brakes the whole time. Watch out for wildlife crossing the road, especially in the early morning and at dusk.

blocks.text: Adapting the Plan to Your Group

items.name: Travelling with kids
items.blurb: Focus on the Thai-Danish Dairy Farm, Chokchai Farm, and Primo Piazza where children can feed animals. Scale back the forest hikes inside the national park.

items.name: Nature and hiking focus
items.blurb: Give the full day to Khao Yai — cover Haew Suwat, the viewpoints, and the nature trail network. Cut the cafés and farms.

items.name: Café and photography focus
items.blurb: PB Valley Winery, the mountain-view cafés along Muak Lek and Pak Chong, and Primo Piazza for that European-countryside feel. Just hit one viewpoint in the park and head back down.

blocks.html: Both Khao Yai and Muak Lek are doable year-round, but the feel changes with the season. Rainy season (Jun–Oct) brings lush green hills and powerful waterfalls — roads can get slippery and afternoon rain is common. Cool season (Nov–Feb) is when the park is at its most beautiful: fresh air, morning mist, sometimes single-digit temperatures on the hilltops. It's also the most crowded, so book accommodation well ahead. Hot season waterfalls drop in volume, but Muak Lek is still swimmable and the park sees fewer visitors.

faq.q: Can you really cover both Saraburi and Khao Yai in the same trip?
faq.a: Yes, quite comfortably. They're on the same road — Highway 2 (Mittraphap Road) runs straight through both. Day one, collect Saraburi's highlights (Phra Phutthabat Temple, Muak Lek Waterfall, the dairy farm), sleep near Muak Lek or Pak Chong, and push into Khao Yai on day two. No backtracking needed.

faq.q: Where's the best place to sleep if I want to be at Khao Yai early the next morning?
faq.a: Stay near Pak Chong or along Route 2090 (Thanarat Road) leading up to the park. That puts you close to the gate. Sleeping in central Saraburi means an extra hour of driving up in the morning, which eats into your cool, quiet park time.

faq.q: How much is the Khao Yai National Park entry fee?
faq.a: For Thai nationals: adults around 40 THB, children around 20 THB. There's a separate vehicle fee on top of that. Foreign visitors pay a higher rate. The park opens around 08:00. Always check the current rates when you arrive — they can change.

faq.q: Is this trip possible without a car?
faq.a: It's possible but takes more planning. Take a bus or minivan from Bangkok to Pak Chong, then either rent a car locally or hire a day-use minivan with a driver. The attractions inside the park and out on the farms are too spread out to manage on foot or by local transport alone.

faq.q: Can this be done as a one-day trip?
faq.a: Technically yes, but it'll feel rushed and tiring once you factor in drive time. If you only have one day, focus on one destination — either Saraburi or Khao Yai — and do it properly. The two-day format is the right amount of time to enjoy both without feeling like you're just ticking boxes.
